requirements.text:
clamp(x, lo, hi) reads its arguments as signed integers. It returns lo when x < lo, else hi
when x > hi, else x.
requirements.reason: The claim covers every 32-bit input triple and uses signed comparisons to return the lower bound, upper bound, or x as required.

requirements.text:
gcd(a, b) reads its arguments as unsigned integers and returns their greatest common divisor,
with gcd(a, 0) = a.
requirements.reason: The claim interprets both inputs as unsigned values and returns their greatest common divisor; this includes gcd(a, 0) = a.

requirements.text: sum_to(n) reads n as an unsigned integer and returns 0 + 1 + ... + (n - 1), wrapped to 32 bits.
requirements.reason: The claim sums the unsigned values from zero up to n − 1 and converts the result to 32 bits, so it wraps as required.

claims.summary: For every 32-bit input, the sum_to export returns the sum of the integers below its unsigned value, reduced to 32 bits.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Covers every 32-bit input, interpreted as unsigned for the range bound.
The expected result is the sum of integers from zero up to, but not including, that bound, wrapped to 32 bits.
Returns adds that the module can be instantiated, and every call in a fresh instance under every host behavior terminates without a trap and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The list range is over the unsigned interpretation of the 32-bit input, so the claim does not describe a signed negative bound.
The sum is reduced modulo 2 to the power of 32; it is not an unbounded mathematical sum.
It asserts termination and no trap for every input, which includes very large loop bounds.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, clamp returns the value selected by signed comparisons against the supplied bounds.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent:
`clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` if `x < lo`, else `hi` if `x > hi`, else `x`
(tested in this order, so with `lo > hi` the result is `lo` for `x < lo` and `hi` otherwise).
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit inputs: the value, lower bound, and upper bound.
Comparisons use signed 32-bit order; the selected value is returned unchanged as a 32-bit bit pattern, with no arithmetic wraparound.
Returns adds that the module can be instantiated, and every call in a fresh instance under every host behavior terminates without a trap and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: This is a signed comparison clamp: if the lower bound exceeds the upper bound, the nested comparisons do not enforce a conventional interval clamp; the claim still specifies its exact behavior.
No relationship between the three inputs is assumed.

claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, gcd returns their unsigned greatest common divisor.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, each interpreted as an unsigned number.
The result is their natural-number greatest common divisor, encoded in 32 bits; there is no arithmetic wraparound needed because it fits in 32 bits.
Returns adds that the module can be instantiated, and every call in a fresh instance under every host behavior terminates without a trap and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The inputs are treated as unsigned natural numbers, not signed integers; negative-looking bit patterns therefore denote large positive values.
The claim does not specify signed greatest common divisor behavior.
